cohort: 30,867 women aged 18-55 years delivering at a major academic center between July 2013 and October 2018
finding: Machine learning models, particularly gradient boosted decision trees, can effectively identify women at risk for postpartum hemorrhage using data available before delivery, potentially allowing for preventative measures.
mod_finding: Models stratified by mode of delivery showed good to excellent discrimination in predicting postpartum hemorrhage but lacked sufficient sensitivity for clinical use.
